hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y (positive steady-state gain): a sustained u>0 drives y above its starting value.
Response has inertia: y does not jump instantly but follows with lag/time-constant on order tens to low hundreds of seconds.
No large dead-zone: u around 0.3-0.4 produces a measurable positive slope, falsified if y stays flat at this level.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.15-0.17 due to heat loss to the room.
Steady-state y is monotonically increasing and approximately linear in u, with the u needed to hold 0.5 in the mid-range 0.2-0.7.
Sensor noise is small relative to control band width 0.05; repeated readings at settled conditions vary by <0.01.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Direction/magnitude of gain and lag: a mid-level long hold separates positive-gain with inertia from dead-zone/no-response and gives first slope and curvature for settling time.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is 0.1687 + 0.006*0.4*250 = 0.7687, which stays below soft limit 0.85 with ~0.08 margin, so even with no decay or lag the limit cannot be reached.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y should rise monotonically from ~0.17 after a short lag/delay, with positive slope that gradually flattens as heat loss grows, ending clearly above start but well below soft limit.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero completed experiments: gain magnitude, lag, dead-zone, u=0 decay rate, linearity, steady-state u for 0.5, and noise are all unresolved, so no controller can be justified yet.
proposal.operator_note: First heating test at 40% power to measure rise rate, lag and approximate gain.

submission.machine_card: Heater: positive gain, no dead-zone. y_ss ~0.175+1.1*u. u=0.3 holds ~0.505, u=0.2 heads to ~0.395, u=0.4 heads to ~0.61, u=0 decays to ambient ~0.15-0.20. Inertia tau ~150-250s, settling ~450-600s, negligible pure delay. Self-draining: falls on its own at u=0 from 0.54 to 0.19 in 480s. Speed max ~0.006/s per unit u. Noise: baseline +-0.02 plus intermittent large negative dropouts 0.05-0.07 (E1,E2,E4,E5,E7,E8) large vs 0.05 band, must filter. Target 0.5 needs u~0.29-0.30.
submission.design_rationale: First-order heat-loss model y_ss=amb+K*u with amb~0.175 K~1.1 from E5 settled 0.505 at u=0.3, E2 ambient ~0.175 at u=0, E1/E8 consistent. Tau ~150-250s (still rising after 250-360s, settled after ~540s) so closed-loop Tc~90s via Kp=0.9 gives settling <300s. Feedforward u_ff=(target-amb)/K gives correct bias ~0.296 for 0.5; P halves residual FF error, I trims rest. I gated to |e|<0.15 and limited to +-0.20 in u (int_lim 25 with Ki=0.008) to prevent windup during 0.32 initial error while leaving authority for >0.1 FF error. EMA tau_f=12s smooths +-0.02 noise; single-sample dips -0.05 to -0.07 rejected by -0.04/+0.06 outlier gate with 0.1x update to avoid kick and energy waste. Saturation back-calculation + yf>0.84 cut to 0 protects 0.9 hard cutoff.
submission.predicted_behavior: From ambient ~0.18 to 0.5: rise at ~0.0035/s, enters 0.475-0.525 in ~180-250s, settled by 300s. True overshoot <0.015, no oscillation. Steady u ~0.29-0.31 (0.296 nominal). After settling, true stays within +-0.01, noisy y mostly in band except rejected dips. Energy near minimum: steady u^2 ~0.09.
self_test_expectations: control returns finite u in [0,1] for y in [0,1], dt 0.05-20s, first call with {}
